description: The plot illustrates the normalized average gate value assigned to experts across different task categories as the number of experts increases from 1 to 64, with the x-axis displayed on a logarithmic scale and labeled “Experts,” and the y-axis labeled “Normalized Average Gate Value,” ranging from 0.00 to 0.20. Each solid line represents a distinct task—Intent (orange), Summary (blue), Law (yellow), Translation (purple), Math (gray), and Code (green)—while the dashed black line labeled “Uniform” indicates an even distribution across experts. For all tasks, the gate value starts high at 1 expert (e.g., Translation ~0.17, Intent ~0.07) and declines sharply as the number of experts increases, approaching near-zero values by 64 experts. The shaded regions surrounding each solid line indicate variance across model layers, with wider shading at lower expert counts (especially for Translation) suggesting greater layer-wise inconsistency. The “Uniform” line remains flat at approximately 0.02 across all expert counts, serving as a baseline for comparison. The steep drop in gate values for task-specific lines suggests that only a small subset of experts dominate the gating decisions, reinforcing the paper’s claim of expert specialization.
